chapter.li: Verse6 Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, VerseEnd Verse7 there came unto him a woman having an alabaster box of very precious ointment, and poured it on his head as he sat in the house. VerseEnd Verse8 But when some saw this, they had indignation, saying, Unto what purpose is this waste? VerseEnd Verse9 For this ointment might have been sold for much and given to the poor. VerseEnd Verse10 When they had said thus, Jesus understood them, and he said unto them, Why trouble you the woman? For she has wrought a good work upon me. VerseEnd Verse11 For you have the poor always with you, but me you have not always. VerseEnd Verse12 For she has poured this ointment on my body for my burial, and in this thing that she has done, she shall be blessed; VerseEnd Verse13 for truly I say unto you, wherever this gospel shall be preached in the whole world, this thing that this woman has done shall also be told for a memorial of her. VerseEnd

Verse14 Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests VerseEnd Verse15 and said, What will you give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver. VerseEnd Verse16 And from that time, he sought opportunity to betray Jesus. VerseEnd

Verse17 Now on the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came unto Jesus, saying unto him, Where do you desire that we prepare for you to eat the passover? VerseEnd Verse18 And he said, Go into the city to such a man and say unto him, The Master says, My time is at hand, I will keep the Passover at your house with my disciples. VerseEnd Verse19 And the disciples did as Jesus appointed them, and they made ready the passover. VerseEnd

Verse20 Now when the evening came, he sat down with the twelve. VerseEnd Verse21 And as they did eat, he said, Truly I say unto you that one of you shall betray me. VerseEnd Verse22 And they were exceedingly sorrowful, and began every one of them to say unto him, Lord, is it I? VerseEnd Verse23 And he answered and said, He that dips his hand with me in the dish, the same shall betray me, VerseEnd Verse24 but the Son of Man goes as it is written of him. But woe unto that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed. It would have been good for that man if he had not been born. VerseEnd Verse25 Then Judas, who betrayed him, answered and said, Master, is it I? He said unto him, You have said. VerseEnd

Verse26 And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and broke it, and blessed it, and gave to his disciples, and said, Take, eat. This is in remembrance of my body, which I gave a ransom for you. VerseEnd Verse27 And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, Drink you all of it, VerseEnd Verse28 for this is in remembrance of my blood of the new covenant, which is shed for as many as shall believe on my name, for the remission of their sins. VerseEnd

Verse29 And I give unto you a commandment that you shall observe to do the things which you have seen me do, and bear record of me, even unto the end. But I say unto you, I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom. VerseEnd

Verse30 And when they had sung a hymn, they went out into the Mount of Olives. VerseEnd Verse31 Then said Jesus unto them, All you shall be offended because of me this night; for it is written: I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad. VerseEnd Verse32 But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee. VerseEnd Verse33 Peter answered and said unto him, Though all men shall be offended because of you, I will never be offended. VerseEnd Verse34 Jesus said unto him, Truly I say unto you that this night, before the cock crows, you shall deny me three times. VerseEnd Verse35 Peter said unto him, Though I should die with you, yet will I not deny you. Likewise also said all the disciples. VerseEnd

Verse36 Then comes Jesus with them unto a place called Gethsemane, and said unto the disciples, Sit here while I go and pray over there. VerseEnd Verse37 And he took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and very heavy. VerseEnd Verse38 Then said he unto them, My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even unto death. Wait here and watch with me. VerseEnd

Verse39 And he went a little further, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me; nevertheless, not as I will, but as you will. VerseEnd Verse40 And he came unto the disciples and found them asleep, and he said unto Peter, What, could you not watch with me one hour? VerseEnd Verse41 Watch, and pray that you enter not into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak. VerseEnd Verse42 He went away again the second time and prayed, saying, O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me except I drink it, your will be done. VerseEnd Verse43 And he came and found them asleep again, for their eyes were heavy. VerseEnd Verse44 And he left them, and went away again, and prayed the third time, saying the same words. VerseEnd Verse45 Then he came to his disciples and said unto them, Sleep on now, and take rest. Behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners. VerseEnd

Verse46 And after they had slept, he said unto them, Arise, and let us be going. Behold, he is at hand that does betray me. VerseEnd Verse47 And while he yet spoke, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and elders of the people. VerseEnd Verse48 Now he that betrayed him gave them a sign, saying, Whomever I shall kiss, that same is he. Hold him fast. VerseEnd Verse49 And immediately he came to Jesus and said, Hail, Master, and kissed him. VerseEnd Verse50 And Jesus said unto him, Judas, why have you come to betray me with a kiss?

Then came they and laid hands on Jesus and took him. VerseEnd Verse51 And behold, one of them who was with Jesus stretched out his hand and drew his sword, and struck a servant of the high priest, and smote off his ear. VerseEnd Verse52 Then said Jesus unto him, Put up again your sword into its place, for all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword. VerseEnd Verse53 Do you think that I cannot now pray to my Father and he shall presently give me more than twelve legions of angels? VerseEnd Verse54 But how then shall the scriptures be fulfilled, that thus it must be? VerseEnd

Verse55 In that same hour said Jesus unto the multitudes, Are you come out as against a thief with swords and staves in order to take me? I sat daily with you in the temple, teaching, and you laid no hold on me. VerseEnd Verse56 But all this was done that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples forsook him and fled. VerseEnd

Verse57 And they that had laid hold on Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were assembled. VerseEnd Verse58 But Peter followed him afar off unto the high priest’s palace, and went in, and sat with the servants to see the end. VerseEnd

Verse59 Now the chief priests, and elders, and all the council, sought false witness against Jesus, to put him to death, VerseEnd Verse60 but found none. Yea, though many false witnesses came, they found none that could accuse him. At the last, came two false witnesses VerseEnd Verse61 and said, This man said, I am able to destroy the temple of God and to build it in three days. VerseEnd Verse62 And the high priest arose and said unto him, Do you answer nothing? Do you know what these witness against you? VerseEnd Verse63 But Jesus held his peace.

And the high priest answered and said unto him, I adjure you by the living God that you tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God. VerseEnd Verse64 Jesus said unto him, You have said. Nevertheless, I say unto you, hereafter shall you see the Son of Man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of Heaven. VerseEnd Verse65 Then the high priest rent his clothes, saying, He has spoken blasphemy. What further need have we of witnesses? Behold, now you have heard his blasphemy. VerseEnd Verse66 What do you think? They answered and said, He is guilty of death. VerseEnd Verse67 Then they did spit in his face, and buffeted him, and others smote him with the palms of their hands, VerseEnd Verse68 saying, Prophesy unto us, you Christ. Who is it that smote you? VerseEnd

Verse69 Now Peter sat outside in the palace, and a damsel came unto him, saying, You also were with Jesus of Galilee. VerseEnd Verse70 But he denied before them all, saying, I know not what you say. VerseEnd Verse71 And when he had gone out into the porch, another saw him and said unto them that were there, This man was also with Jesus of Nazareth. VerseEnd Verse72 And again he denied, with an oath, saying, I do not know the man. VerseEnd Verse73 And after a while came they that stood by and said to Peter, Surely you also are one of them, for your speech betrays you. VerseEnd Verse74 Then began he to curse and to swear, saying, I know not the man. And immediately the cock crowed. VerseEnd Verse75 And Peter remembered the words of Jesus, which he said unto him: Before the cock crows, you shall deny me three times. And he went out and wept bitterly. VerseEnd

LEChapter27 Verse1 When the morning came, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death. VerseEnd Verse2 And when they had bound him, they led him away and delivered him to Pontius Pilate the governor. VerseEnd

Verse3 Then Judas, who had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, regretted it and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, VerseEnd Verse4 saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said unto him, What is that to us? You see to it; your sins be upon you. VerseEnd Verse5 And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple and departed, and went and hanged himself on a tree. And immediately he fell down, and his bowels gushed out, and he died. VerseEnd

Verse6 And the chief priests took the silver pieces and said, It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood. VerseEnd Verse7 And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter’s field, to bury strangers in. VerseEnd Verse8 Wherefore, that field was called, The field of blood, unto this day. VerseEnd Verse9 Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet, saying, And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was valued, whom they of the children of Israel did VerseEnd Verse10 value. And therefore they took the pieces of silver and gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord appointed by the mouth of Jeremiah. VerseEnd

Verse11 And Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor asked him, saying, Are you the king of the Jews? And Jesus said unto him, You say truly, for thus it is written of me. VerseEnd Verse12 And when he was accused of the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing. VerseEnd Verse13 Then said Pilate unto him, Do you not hear how many things they witness against you? VerseEnd Verse14 And he answered him not to his questions; yea, never a word, insomuch that the governor marveled greatly. VerseEnd

Verse15 Now at the feast, the governor was accustomed to release unto the people a prisoner, whom they desired. VerseEnd Verse16 And they had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas. VerseEnd Verse17 Therefore, when they had gathered together, Pilate said unto them, Whom do you desire that I release unto you? Barabbas? Or Jesus who is called Christ? VerseEnd (Verse18 For he knew that for envy they had delivered him. VerseEnd Verse19 When he was seated on the judgment seat, his wife sent unto him, saying, Have nothing to do with that just man, for I have suffered many things this day in a vision because of him. VerseEnd)

Verse20 But the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude that they should ask Barabbas and destroy Jesus. VerseEnd Verse21 And the governor said unto them, Which of the two do you desire that I release unto you? They said, Barabbas. VerseEnd Verse22 Pilate said unto them, What shall I do with Jesus, who is called Christ? And all said unto him, Let him be crucified. VerseEnd Verse23 And the governor said, Why? What evil has he done? But they cried out the more, saying, Let him be crucified! VerseEnd Verse24 When Pilate saw that he could prevail nothing, but rather a tumult was made, he took water and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person. See that you do nothing unto him. VerseEnd Verse25 Then answered all the people and said, His blood come on us and our children. VerseEnd Verse26 Then he released Barabbas unto them. And when he had scourged Jesus, he delivered him to be crucified. VerseEnd

Verse27 Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the common hall, and gathered unto him the whole band, VerseEnd Verse28 and they stripped him, and put on him a purple robe. VerseEnd Verse29 And when they had plaited a crown of thorns, they put it upon his head and a reed in his right hand. And they bowed the knee before him and they mocked him, saying, Hail, king of the Jews! VerseEnd Verse30 And they spit upon him, and took the reed and smote him on the head. VerseEnd Verse31 And after they had mocked him, they took the robe off from him, and put his own raiment on him, and led him away to crucify him. VerseEnd Verse32 And as they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name; him they compelled to bear his cross. VerseEnd

Verse33 And when they had come unto a place called Golgotha — that is to say, a place of burial VerseEnd — Verse34 they gave him vinegar to drink, mingled with gall. And when he had tasted the vinegar, he would not drink. VerseEnd Verse35 And they crucified him and parted his garments, casting lots, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet: They parted my garments among them, and for my vesture they did cast lots. VerseEnd Verse36 And sitting down, they watched him there. VerseEnd

Verse37 And Pilate wrote a title and put it on the cross. And the writing was: jesus of nazareth, the king of the jews, in letters of Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew. And the chief priest said unto Pilate, It should be written and set up over his head his accusation: This is he that said he was Jesus, the king of the Jews. But Pilate answered and said, What I have written, I have written. Let it alone. VerseEnd Verse38 Then were there two thieves crucified with him, one on the right hand and another on the left. VerseEnd

Verse39 And they that passed by reviled him, wagging their heads VerseEnd Verse40 and saying, You that destroy the temple and build it again in three days, save yourself. If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross. VerseEnd Verse41 Likewise also the chief priests, mocking with the scribes and elders, said, VerseEnd Verse42 He saved others, himself he cannot save. If he is the king of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him. VerseEnd Verse43 He trusted in God, let him deliver him now. If he will save him, let him save him, for he said, I am the Son of God. VerseEnd

Verse44 One of the thieves also, who was crucified with him, reviled him in like manner. But the other rebuked him, saying, Do you not fear God, seeing you are under the same condemnation, and this man is just and has not sinned? And he cried unto the Lord that he would save him. And the Lord said unto him, This day you shall be with me in the world of spirits. VerseEnd

Verse45 Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour. VerseEnd Verse46 And about the ninth hour, Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? (That is to say, My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? VerseEnd) Verse47 Some of them that stood there, when they heard him, said, This man calls for Elijah. VerseEnd Verse48 And immediately one of them ran and took a sponge, and filled it with vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink. VerseEnd Verse49 The rest said, Let him be; let us see whether Elijah will come to save him. VerseEnd
Verse50 Jesus, when he had cried again with a loud voice — saying, Father, it is finished; your will is done! — yielded up the ghost. VerseEnd

Verse51 And behold, the veil of the temple was rent in two, from the top to the bottom. And the earth did quake, and the rocks rent. VerseEnd Verse52 And the graves were opened, and the bodies of the saints which slept arose, VerseEnd Verse53 who were many, and came out of the graves, and after his resurrection went into the holy city and appeared unto many. VerseEnd

Verse54 Now when the centurions, and they that were with him watching Jesus, heard the earthquake and saw those things which were done, they feared greatly, saying, Truly this was the Son of God. VerseEnd Verse55 And many women were there beholding afar off, who followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering unto him for his burial, VerseEnd Verse56 among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee’s children. VerseEnd

Verse57 When the evening came, there came a rich man of Arimathea named Joseph, who also himself was Jesus’ disciple. VerseEnd Verse58 He went to Pilate and begged the body of Jesus. Then Pilate commanded the body to be delivered. VerseEnd Verse59 And when Joseph had taken the body, he wrapped it in a clean linen cloth VerseEnd Verse60 and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock. And he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulcher and departed. VerseEnd Verse61 And there was Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting opposite the sepulcher. VerseEnd

Verse62 Now the next day that followed the day of the preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees came together unto Pilate, VerseEnd Verse63 saying, Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again. VerseEnd Verse64 Command therefore that the sepulcher be made sure until the third day, lest his disciples come by night and steal him away, and say unto the people, He is risen from the dead, so this last imposture will be worse than the first. VerseEnd Verse65 Pilate said unto them, You have a watch; go your way, make it as sure as you can. VerseEnd Verse66 So they went and made the sepulcher sure, sealing the stone and setting a watch. VerseEnd
